correctness.rationale: On full U(n) with normalized Haar measure, the unit symmetrization of e_1⊗…⊗e_n has diagonal matrix coefficient perm(U) in Sym^n(C^n): each of the n! summands in the bra contributes the same sum of permanent monomials. This irreducible representation has dimension binom(2n−1,n); the Haar average of the rank-one projector is the identity divided by that dimension. Scalar phase invariance gives mean zero, so the second moment is the variance. The ratio equals the product of (n+j)/n over j=0,…,n−1, strictly above one for n≥2 and one at n=1; Stirling's ratio Γ(2n)/[Γ(n)n^n] gives the stated 2^(−1/2)(4/e)^n. The central-binomial estimate gives the stated RMS, and Markov gives exactly q(n)/R_n for any fixed positive polynomial q. Rivin v3 really applies the erroneous variance to the entire Haar unitary; §8.3 separately writes n!/poly(n) as the PACC threshold and then argues using σ²/poly(n). The original review claim controls the latter variance-based scale (and a fortiori the larger threshold on a literal full-Haar reading); it does not identify these two source thresholds or refute Gaussian-submatrix PACC. No conclusion about Gaussian shape at correct full-Haar scale. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and artifacts/verify.py; finite arithmetic script not run or needed for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The correction reverses a specific published-in-preprint probability inference for a standard ensemble, from near one to exponentially small even with any polynomial slack. It sets the RMS benchmark necessary to interpret full-Haar numerical experiments and avoids transferring a Gaussian-entry conjecture to a different ensemble at an incompatible scale. The specific quantitative error and its consequence justify the correction; the standalone classical identity or generic use of Markov would not.
